_README: Things about you that tools need and that change rarely.
Copy to vault/settings/profile.json and edit. The whole file is optional.
This example exists because tools/settings_drift.py found it missing on the day it was
written: vault/settings/profile.json was created 2026-08-26 and no example shipped beside
it, so nobody cloning this repo could discover the file existed at all. A setting nobody
can find is a setting nobody sets.
'spelling' drives tools/cv_lint.py, and ABSENT MEANS OFF -- deliberately. The rules moved
out of the shipped code because the linter was enforcing Ireland/UK conventions on
everybody: a US candidate writing a correct US CV got a finding for every 'optimize' and
'center', a non-zero exit, and no flag to turn it off. Enforcing a spelling nobody declared
was the original bug, so the default had to be silence rather than a guess.
Values: 'ie-uk' | 'us' | 'off'. Anything else is treated as 'off'.
🔴 Delete the line below rather than leaving it as it stands. The angle brackets are not a
value: they match no locale, so the linter falls back to 'off' and quietly checks nothing.
'working_days_per_year' annualises a contract day rate. Yours, not a market constant -- it is
how many days you would actually bill after annual leave. 220 is a common answer in Ireland
and the UK; 250 is the year with no leave at all and will overstate a contract by about 14%.
Omit it and nothing will annualise a rate for you rather than guessing one.
working_days_per_year: <how many days would you actually bill in a year? 220 allows for annual leave>
